summary: Thorough specialized-service assessment with strong subgroup evidence; its main constraint is that match rates among completed trips cannot estimate request fulfillment for New Yorkers overall.

artifactRatings.rationale: The completed-trip calculations are coherent, but the headline 100% WAV match is structurally selected and cannot answer population-level availability without canceled or unfulfilled requests.
Methods, metrics, comparisons, citywide evidence, geography, time, provider variation, context, and limitations are all present.
Flag definitions, validity windows, confidence intervals, denominator audits, and metric-specific filters are explicit.
Counts, cross-flag audits, subgroup sample sizes, and source field definitions make the conclusions traceable.
Selection bias and the limits of operator-reported match flags are prominently and correctly reflected in the assessment.

strengths: Audits match-without-request rows instead of silently changing denominators.
Uses wait and geographic variation when WAV match labels have no variation.
concerns: The task wording is broader than completed-trip indicators can resolve; all-request and cancellation data are essential.
